candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss per R decreases as the accessible specific surface area per framework mass (ASA, median-normalized) increases relative to a fixed molecular size scale: frameworks exposing more adsorption surface per mass offer more distinct positional (site) microstates to the adsorbate, preserving configurational entropy, so a larger descriptor value corresponds to smaller entropy loss per R.
candidates.rationale: Connectivity/site-density mechanism: at infinite dilution the adsorbed-phase configurational entropy scales with the number of distinguishable docking sites; ASA per gram is a direct geometric proxy for site-count density on the framework, and the Vol^(1/3) factor encodes that larger molecules resolve finer positional distinctions (fewer effectively distinct sites), increasing entropy loss. This is an inference from lattice/configurational entropy arguments; AV is deliberately not combined with ASA because their native length units differ and reference normalization of each independently avoids silent unit conversion.
candidates.falsification_criteria: In the declared ASA training regime (quantiles 0.1-0.9), finite-difference perturbation of ASA must increase the descriptor (consistency check). Falsified if the training association sign with entropy loss/R contradicts the declared (negative) direction, or if adding the descriptor does not improve MAE of entropy loss/R over the 14-input baseline on held-out training folds beyond noise.

scientific_test.proxy_assumptions: Assumes rigid pure-silica frameworks at infinite dilution; ASA (m^2/g, probe-accessible) is treated as a proxy for the density of distinct adsorption sites; Vol^(1/3) is a representative molecular length that rescales site resolution. No free-volume or mass-normalization model is imposed; ASA and AV are never combined directly. Proxy consistency check only; association may be confounded with pore size.
scientific_test.physical_interpretation: q_ASA and q_Vol are independently median-normalized dimensionless ratios; q_ASA = 1 does not mean the framework surface equals a physical reference area, and the product descriptor has no claim of unit equivalence between the two factors.

dimensional_audit.limitation: Unit algebra does not verify the mechanism or numerical unit conversion.

scientific_check.interpretation: Finite difference checks the declared proxy; training association is observational and may be confounded.

candidates.name: molecular_aperture_fit
candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss per R increases with the ratio of the adsorbate's largest interatomic span (GeDi, median-normalized) to the framework's largest free-sphere diameter (lsd_f, median-normalized): molecules whose longest dimension approaches or exceeds the widest accessible aperture must adopt a reduced set of translational and orientational configurations, so a larger descriptor value corresponds to larger entropy loss per R.
candidates.rationale: Translation/shape-coupling mechanism: while Vol^(1/3) is an isotropic size proxy (used in retained candidates), GeDi captures the extreme molecular dimension that actually matters for passing through and reorienting within apertures; a large span relative to the widest free sphere forces near-single-file configurations and suppresses rotational microstates. This is a new combination motivated by transition-state/free-sphere arguments in molecular sieving (inference), not an established law for this dataset.
candidates.falsification_criteria: In the declared lsd_f training regime (quantiles 0.1-0.9), finite-difference perturbation of lsd_f must decrease the descriptor (consistency check). Falsified if the training Spearman sign between descriptor and entropy loss/R contradicts the declared (positive) direction, or if adding the descriptor as an extra input does not reduce MAE of entropy loss/R versus the 14-input baseline on held-out training folds beyond noise.

scientific_test.proxy_assumptions: Assumes rigid pure-silica frameworks at infinite dilution; lsd_f from geometric probes approximates the widest accessible aperture; GeDi is treated as the critical molecular length for aperture passage and reorientation, an inference since real docking geometries depend on orientation. The ratio is not a clearance measure: q_GeDi/q_lsd_f = 1 does not mean GeDi equals lsd_f physically because the normalizations use independent training medians.
scientific_test.physical_interpretation: q_GeDi and q_lsd_f are separately median-normalized dimensionless ratios; both numerator and denominator are positive geometric lengths in angstroms so their ratio is dimensionless, but the reference scales differ (molecular vs framework), so threshold-one readings carry no physical equality claim.

dimensional_audit.limitation: Unit algebra does not verify the mechanism or numerical unit conversion.

scientific_check.interpretation: Finite difference checks the declared proxy; training association is observational and may be confounded.

retained.name: confinement_length_ratio
retained.hypothesis: For pure-silica zeolites at infinite dilution, the entropy loss (s_ads/s_gas, in units of R) decreases as the ratio of the largest free-sphere path diameter to the adsorbate cubic length scale decreases; i.e., tighter confinement relative to molecular size (small descriptor value) correlates with larger entropy loss per R.

retained.name: accessible_space_index
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss per R decreases as the total accessible pore space per framework mass (AV, median-normalized) and the largest free-sphere path diameter jointly increase relative to the adsorbate size: frameworks offering more and wider accessible volume preserve more translational and orientational microstates, so a larger descriptor value corresponds to smaller entropy loss per R.
